rule: PR requires the local review gate to hold when local review ran
description: P3 coupling. `plugin/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements) is the single home of the local review gate: which local review exit reasons hold the gate before a PR opens, and that every other exit reason holds nothing. The source pin is ONE span carrying both halves of that claim: the holding set (`clean`, and `diminishing-returns` once its advisory exit is taken) and the obligation on the rest (every other exit reason holds nothing, max-iterations-reached included, and stops the PR on every path). Adding a third holding exit reason inside the sentence, dropping the advisory-exit condition on `diminishing-returns`, rewriting `holds nothing`, dropping the max-iterations-reached example, or narrowing `on every path` turns the suite red. A consumer in the same file pins the discriminating condition and its obligation as ONE span: when local review ran on the branch, the PR opens only when the last exit reason it returned holds the gate. Dropping the ran-on-the-branch condition, or keying the gate on an exit reason other than the last one, turns the suite red. A second consumer in the same file pins the not-run clause: local review that did not run, because it is not configured or was skipped, neither holds nor blocks the PR, so rewriting a skipped review into a blocker or into a hold turns the suite red. Two consumers in `plugin/skills/open-plan-pr/SKILL.md` pin the pointers to the canonical section, a Before checklist item and a Do Not bullet, each naming `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements); they pin the reference, not the rule, so the skill restates no exit reason. Deleting a pointer or retargeting its file or section turns the suite red. What these pins honestly guarantee is exactly that these five word sequences exist in these two named files; they claim nothing about meaning and nothing about what the workflow script, the state machine, or an agent actually does. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a meaning inversion around the pinned bytes, such as a later sentence in the section that names a further holding exit reason or exempts a path, is invisible; (2) agreement between this statement and the engines' own routing tables is not checked here, because a presence pin cannot compare two tables; (3) the Do Not bullet's negation comes from the `## Do Not` heading, not from the pinned sentence, and the heading is unpinned; (4) the `expect_commit` sentence in the skill, by which a caller's local review check stands in for the skill's own, is unpinned; (5) a NEW PR-opening path that never carries a pointer to the canonical section is an absence defect no fixture in this directory can see, per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract.

source.pattern: The exit reasons that hold the gate are `clean`, and `diminishing-returns` once its advisory exit is taken. Every other exit reason holds nothing, max-iterations-reached included, and stops the PR on every path: the workflow script, the state machine, and any step taken outside both.

consumers.pattern: Local review gate: when local review ran on the branch, the PR opens only when the last exit reason it returned holds the gate.
Local review that did not run, because it is not configured or was skipped, neither holds nor blocks the PR.
- [ ] Local review gate held, or local review did not run, per `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements)
- open PR when local review ran on the branch and did not hold the local review gate per `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements)
